transcript.text: Samsung RS67A8810S9 fridge freezer display says OF OF and everything is getting warm. Fan's quiet. Has it broken?
A door left ajar or a big shop of warm food can take a fridge freezer a day to recover. Has a door been left open or not shut properly recently, or has a lot of warm food gone in?

No, no doors left open as far as I know. The kids were pressing the buttons on the panel yesterday though, and this morning everything was warm. The fridge is 9C now and I'm worried about the milk and chicken.

Thanks for confirming the doors were kept shut. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is set to about 3–5°C and the freezer to -18°C, and make sure no holiday or eco mode is active. You can refer to the picture shown in the app for guidance on where these controls are located. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

The display just says OF OF, there's no temperature showing, so I can't tell what it's set to. Is OF OF something the kids have switched on by pressing the buttons? I don't have a dial, only the touch panel.

Cold air enters through vents, usually on the back wall inside. Please ensure food isn't pressed against them and that shelves aren't packed so tightly that air cannot move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?

I haven't checked the vents, but nothing's been moved or packed in differently recently. It's still showing OF OF though and the fridge is 9C. Is OF OF something the kids could have switched on? I'm worried about the milk and chicken.

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven't had a chance yet. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
